name: Siam R-CNN (Voigtlaender et al., CVPR 2020) - re-detection and dynamic programming over tracklets of the target and distractors
bibliography: Paul Voigtlaender, Jonathon Luiten, Philip H.S. Torr, Bastian Leibe. Siam R-CNN: Visual Tracking by Re-Detection. CVPR 2020 (peer-reviewed, CVF open access). Preprint: arXiv:1911.12836 (HTML https://arxiv.org/html/1911.12836 ; same study, includes long appendix with per-attribute and VOS results). Code: https://github.com/VisualComputingInstitute/SiamR-CNN (MIT license, TensorFlow 1.15 + tensorpack; TDPA implemented as 'ThreeStageTracker' in tracking/three_stage_tracker.py). Builds on Faster R-CNN / Cascade R-CNN (tensorpack implementation) and the PReMVOS embedding network for hard example mining (separate studies).
full_text_checked: arXiv HTML read to ~100k of 120k characters (method Sec. 3.1-3.5, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-8, appendix A-B incl. Tables 9 and 11); the remaining appendix fragment (VOS tables) checked for hyperparameters - none present. Code: README and tracking/three_stage_tracker.py (constructor defaults and _track DP loop) read via raw GitHub. Numeric values of alpha/beta/gamma/w_ff/w_loc are not printed in the paper; taken from code defaults, mapping of code names to paper symbols is my inference.
task_and_output: Generic single-object tracking, short- and long-term, and (with Box2Seg) semi-supervised video object segmentation. Input: first-frame box. Output per frame: one box with a score; if the selected tracklet has no detection in the current frame the object is reported absent (for benchmarks needing a box, the last box is repeated with score 0). Internally: all re-detections of objects similar to the template in the full frame, grouped into tracklets, and a dynamic-programming score per tracklet.
data_and_independent_videos: Training: ImageNet VID (4000 videos), YouTube-VOS 2018 (3471), GOT-10k (9335), LaSOT (1120) = ~18k videos + 119k COCO images; GOT-10k result uses a model trained only on GOT-10k. TDPA hyperparameters tuned once on DAVIS 2017 train. Evaluation on unseen test sets of: OTB2015 (100), UAV123 (123), NfS (100), TrackingNet (511 test), LaSOT test (280), GOT-10k test (180, unseen classes), VOT2018 (60), LTB35 / VOT2018-LT (35), OxUvA (366 test), DAVIS 2017 val, YouTube-VOS val.
target_size_and_input_resolution: Whole frame processed (no search window): Faster R-CNN short edge 800 px (half-resolution variant: short edge 400, max 667 px), ResNet-101-FPN; RoI Align features of 1000 RPN proposals + up to 100 previous detections. Target size arbitrary (any size in the full image); no lattice of the target; template = RoI features of the first-frame box.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Native benchmark frame rates (mostly 25-30 fps, NfS at 30 fps version); arbitrary camera motion; no motion model besides the location-jump penalty and spatial gating between consecutive detections. Runs at 4.7 FPS (13.6-15.2 FPS fast variants) on a GPU.
detector_and_exemplar: Yes: a COCO-pretrained Faster R-CNN/Cascade R-CNN (frozen backbone and RPN) provides class-agnostic proposals; a 3-stage cascade re-detection head decides 'same as template or not' by concatenating template and proposal RoI features. Exemplar = first-frame ground-truth box (never updated), plus the most recent box of the first-frame tracklet used as a second reference in TDPA.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Trained: the 3-stage cascade re-detection head (no weight sharing) on frozen ResNet-101-FPN + RPN; loss = standard Cascade R-CNN classification + box regression with 2 classes (loss name not stated in the text read) [uncertain]. Video hard example mining: negatives retrieved from other videos by nearest-neighbour search in a PReMVOS embedding (batch-hard triplet loss, trained separately); 10k neighbours per step (50k for LaSOT), positives from 30 frames of the reference video. Schedule 1M + 120k + 80k steps, +160k steps with hard examples. TDPA is hand-designed (no learning; 6 hyperparameters tuned on DAVIS 2017 train). Parameter count of the head not given.
controls_seeds_splits: Table 7 ablations on OTB2015 / LaSOT / LTB35 against the full model: no hard example mining, Argmax (per-frame highest re-detection score instead of TDPA), Short-term (previous-box-centred variant with shifted RoIs), resolution/RoI/backbone reductions; Table 9 more speed variants; Table 11 per-attribute OTB deltas incl. 0/100/10000 RoIs. Seeds not reported; single runs; no confidence intervals. Hyperparameters tuned on DAVIS 2017 train, separate from all evaluated tracking benchmarks.
metrics_and_numbers: Table 7 (FPS; OTB2015 AUC; LaSOT AUC; LTB35 F): full 4.7; 70.1; 64.8; 66.8 | no hard example mining 4.7; 68.4; 63.2; 66.5 | Argmax (no TDPA) 4.9; 63.8; 62.9; 65.5 | Short-term 4.6; 67.2; 55.7; 57.2 | half res + 100 RoIs 13.6; 69.1; 63.2; 66.0 | ResNet-50 5.1; 68.0; 62.3; 64.4 | ResNet-50 + half res + 100 RoIs 15.2; 67.7; 61.1; 63.7. TDPA vs Argmax: +6.3 OTB, +1.9 LaSOT, +1.3 LTB35. Table 11 OTB attribute deltas vs full: Argmax -6.3, Short-term -2.8, no HEM -1.7, 0 extra RoIs -12.9. Main results: OTB2015 AUC 70.1; UAV123 64.9 (DiMP-50 65.4 - lower); NfS 63.9; TrackingNet success 81.2 / precision 80.0 / norm. 85.4; LaSOT success 64.8, norm. prec. 72.2; GOT-10k AO 64.9; OxUvA MaxGM 72.3 (TPR 70.1, TNR 74.5); LTB35 F 66.8; VOT2018 (reset protocol) EAO 0.140 for the long-term TDPA version vs 0.408 for the short-term variant (Tables 3/8); DAVIS17 val J&F 70.6 (74.8 with fine-tuned Box2Seg). Code defaults (three_stage_tracker.py): tracklet_distance_threshold 0.06, tracklet_merging_threshold 0.3, tracklet_merging_second_best_relative_threshold 0.3, ff_gt_score_weight 0.1, ff_gt_tracklet_score_weight 0.9, location_score_weight 7.0, TRACKLET_KEEP_ALIVE_TIME 1500 frames.
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (all test sets; GOT-10k unseen classes). Target absence: yes (OxUvA TNR 74.5, LTB35 F-score; absent when the best tracklet has no current detection). Similar distractors: yes, motivation and hard-example mining; no dedicated distractor benchmark; qualitative only. Occlusion: yes (long-term benchmarks, OTB occlusion attribute in Table 11). Night/low light: not reported (only OTB illumination-variation attribute in Table 11) [uncertain]. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes, online; tracklets and DP built from its own detections.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: (1) in every frame, re-detect all objects that look like the first-frame template anywhere in the image (class-agnostic proposals + template-conditioned 2-class cascade head trained with hard negatives from other videos); (2) link detections of consecutive frames into tracklets only when the link is unambiguous (best similarity above a threshold and clearly better than the 2nd/3rd, and within a spatial gate), otherwise start a new tracklet - so tracklets of distractors exist in parallel with the target's; (3) score each tracklet by the sum over its frames of 0.1 x similarity to the first-frame template + 0.9 x similarity to the latest box of the first-frame tracklet, and score transitions between tracklets by -7 x L1 box jump; (4) a dynamic program keeps, for every tracklet, the best total score of any chain of non-overlapping tracklets ending in it (gaps up to 1500 frames); (5) output the current box of the argmax-score tracklet; if it has no detection now, the target is absent. The DP is causal; it can 'change its mind' about which chain is the target, but only the current frame's output is emitted. Proposed modification for us (not published): run the same tracklet DP over YOLO detections (or FlyVis map peaks) inside a loss episode, using FlyVis similarity to the exemplar as the unary score.
transfer_limits: (a) Search space: Siam R-CNN searches the whole frame, so distractor tracklets are long and well separated; our FlyVis crop is ~2x the target (721 hexals, target ~9x12 lattice steps) and moves with the Kalman prediction - map peaks inside it do not form long separate tracklets, and the true target can leave the crop. The closest analogue of its proposals in our stand are YOLO26 detections (conf 0.01) around the prediction, not FlyVis peaks. (b) Features: re-detection relies on ResNet-101-FPN RGB RoI features and a big hard-negative mining pipeline; 34 FlyVis motion/brightness types on 721 grey hexals were never shown to separate same-class neighbours; our tests show FlyVis C/D beat the eye input (R1) but not geometry for identity. (c) Unary dominated by tracklet-reference similarity (0.9) - it trusts the most recent first-frame-tracklet box, i.e. it assumes the tracklet itself was correctly linked; with weak features, wrong linking propagates. (d) Cost: 4.7 FPS on GPU in the original is the detector/head; the DP itself is cheap (number of tracklets within a 30-frame episode is small, O(T x K^2)). For us running FlyVis per candidate box would need a temporal history per candidate (FlyVis is recurrent) - one FlyVis rollout per candidate per episode, i.e. several times the current cost. (e) Episodes <= 30 frames at 30 Hz: TDPA's advantage comes from long histories (LaSOT/LTB35); on short histories its gain vs argmax is smaller (LaSOT +1.9, LTB35 +1.3 vs OTB +6.3 where re-identification after distractor confusion is the issue). (f) In MOT the 'distractors' are other tracks with their own ids; a single-object DP per lost track ignores those assignments unless combined with the ByteTrack cost.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (direct design evidence): distinction between target and distractor is made by sequence-level evidence (tracklet DP), not by the per-frame maximum - Argmax ablation shows per-frame max is worse (-6.3 OTB, -1.9 LaSOT AUC); absence = best chain has no current detection. 5.2 (design analogy): the target model is fixed (first frame) plus the latest tracklet box as a recent view - a two-reference memory without online learning, which avoids drift; distractors are kept as explicit tracklets. 5.3: not addressed (backbone frozen; head trained on detection loss, not through the DP). 5.4 (analogy/caution): it is structurally a tracking-by-detection association over time; in our stand the equivalent effect may be achievable by the MOT tracker itself (ByteTrack/MASA) without FlyVis.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout over time (state transfer) of the centred FlyVis readout during a loss episode. Change: keep, for the lost track, a small set of tracklets of candidates (YOLO detections within the prediction region, or FlyVis map peaks) built with the Siam R-CNN unambiguous-linking rule; unary per frame = 0.1 x FlyVis similarity to the pre-loss exemplar (4 observations) + 0.9 x FlyVis similarity to the latest box of the chain that started at the last confirmed observation; transition = -w x normalized box jump; causal DP; correction only if the argmax chain has a current candidate and its score margin over the second chain exceeds a fixed value, else refuse. Controls: no-FlyVis = identical TDPA with (i) geometry/Kalman only unary, (ii) MASA embedding unary, (iii) R1 eye-input features; stock FlyVis = same TDPA with stock C activity; plus the current centred readout top1 and the per-frame argmax of the same unary (to isolate the DP). Minimal check: on cached train26 episodes (useful-correction fraction per video, paired bootstrap): TDPA_C - argmax_C >= 2 p.p. with lower CI > 0 and TDPA_C - TDPA_geometry and TDPA_C - TDPA_R1 lower CI > 0; refusal precision at fixed coverage. Stop: if TDPA_C does not beat TDPA_geometry or TDPA_MASA (the effect is association-over-time, not FlyVis), or if median episode tracklet count < 2 (nothing to choose), stop before dev/HOTA.
strongest_objection: The gain of TDPA is a gain of temporal association over detections; in our stand that function already exists in ByteTrack/MASA (and in our failed z13_candidate_identity_v1 with expiring distractor identities). If FlyVis features do not separate same-class neighbours, the DP only re-weights geometry and the no-fly TDPA_geometry/TDPA_MASA control will do as well - i.e. it would be an improvement of the tracker, not of FlyVis (rule 6.16). Also, the long-term variant hurt badly under a reset/short-term protocol (VOT2018 EAO 0.140 vs 0.408), showing that re-detection plus sequence-level selection can be harmful when the target is mostly near the previous position - which is our typical case for a short loss.
evidence_strength: Moderate-strong for the published claim: peer-reviewed CVPR 2020, public MIT code (constructor defaults and DP loop verified), many benchmarks with unseen test videos, clear Argmax-vs-TDPA ablation. Weak for transfer: single runs, no intervals, RGB ResNet-101 features, hyperparameters tuned on DAVIS; no evidence with small motion features or within a small moving crop.
where_distinction_is_made: In a separate sequence-level decision (TDPA) over explicit tracklets, on top of a template-conditioned re-detection score. Target found = argmax DP chain has a detection in the current frame; similar distractor = other tracklets with lower chain score (they are explicitly kept and can later win); target outside/absent = argmax chain has no current detection; insufficient data is not modelled separately (ambiguous links simply start new tracklets, deferring the decision). A map/score maximum is distinguished from the right object because the per-frame score enters only as one unary term summed along the chain, plus a location-continuity penalty; the Argmax ablation quantifies the difference.
feature_dependence: Strongly dependent on rich RGB appearance: COCO-pretrained ResNet-101-FPN, cascade head on concatenated RoI features, hard negatives mined with a separate RGB embedding (PReMVOS). Smaller backbone already costs 1.7-2.5 AUC (ResNet-50: OTB 68.0, LaSOT 62.3). No evidence with motion-only or small features; the DP itself is feature-agnostic and could run on any similarity.
association_consequence: Original: single-object output, no detection matching. In our stand: the DP's chosen candidate gives a centre correction (or a direct detection choice) for the lost track before ByteTrack/MASA; refusing keeps the Kalman prediction. Because candidates would be YOLO detections, it would effectively decide matching for the lost track - overlapping with the tracker's own association. External guard alternatives producing a similar effect without the mechanism: Kalman gating plus a maximum-jump limit, and accumulating MASA similarity along candidate tracklets (no FlyVis). For the R1 case (79.7 px shift, cost 0.123 -> 1.0) a jump penalty alone (w_loc term) would likely have blocked the correction [uncertain] - so the no-fly guard is mandatory.
difference_from_tried: Versus z13_candidate_identity_v1 (frame-to-frame Hungarian identity with missing option; argmax-like choice of the carried target id; distractors expire when unmatched): Siam R-CNN differs by (i) global chain scoring over all tracklets with the ability to switch to an older tracklet chain later (DP over tracklets with gaps), (ii) unambiguous-linking rule (start a new tracklet when the 2nd best link is within 0.3) instead of always assigning, (iii) unary combining a fixed first-frame template with the chain's own latest box, (iv) explicit location-jump penalty between tracklets. Versus z13_candidate_ranker_v1 (per-frame learned ranking of 3 peaks): TDPA is precisely the alternative to per-frame selection; its Argmax ablation is the published version of our per-frame choice. Versus observation/query memory: Siam R-CNN does not learn online at all - a different stance. Not tried by us: chain-level DP with delayed decision and multiple hypotheses kept alive. Same as tried: candidate-to-candidate linking by appearance + distance.
memory_write_policy: No learned memory. Fixed first-frame template (never updated) + implicitly the latest box of the first-frame tracklet (updated only when the tracklet is extended by an unambiguous link: best score > 0.3 [uncertain mapping of code threshold] and 2nd/3rd best at least 0.3 lower, within spatial gate). Previous-frame detections are re-inserted as proposals (up to 100). Tracklets kept alive for up to 1500 frames.
distractor_representation: Explicit: every re-detection belongs to some tracklet; distractor tracklets are kept and scored in the DP. Also implicit through hard-negative mining of the re-detection head.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Accumulation over frames: sequence-level DP score over the whole stored history; absence decided per frame as 'the best chain has no detection now'.
loss_on_applied_decision: No: the learned head is trained on per-proposal re-detection (2-class detection loss); the applied decision (TDPA chain selection) is hand-designed and not trained.
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the original (single-object). For us: candidate selection for a lost track among detections (track candidates) or centre correction before matching (state update), with refusal = no change.
no_fly_control_equivalent: The same TDPA with geometry/Kalman-only unary; the same TDPA with MASA appearance embeddings; ByteTrack's own second-stage low-score association with a larger lost-track buffer; a simple maximum-jump/Kalman gate. FlyVis value is only shown if TDPA with FlyVis C beats these and beats TDPA on R1 eye input.
hard_subset_evaluation: No separate hard subset; per-attribute OTB analysis (Table 11) and long-term datasets (LTB35, OxUvA); GOT-10k with unseen classes. Selection by benchmark attribute labels.
temporal_information_availability: Uses only current and past frames; DP updated online each frame; output = current box of the best chain, so latency is zero frames. The DP can re-interpret which past tracklets formed the target, but already emitted outputs are not changed; the method's benefit therefore is available to an online tracker. Note: its benefit grows with history length (gaps up to 1500 frames); within our <= 30-frame episodes much less history is available. Speed 4.7 FPS dominated by the detector/re-detection head, not by the DP.
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields) as set in the item.
